deck_title: Bouguer-Snell n(r)*r*sin(theta) spherical atmospheric refraction invariant vs naive planar Snell drift rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Pierre Bouguer (1729) & Willebrord Snellius (1621) spherical atmospheric refraction law (conserving the Fermat-Noether optical angular momentum / impact parameter p_Bouguer = n(r) * r * sin(theta(r)) = n_0 * r_0 * sin(theta_0) across concentric shells (n*r)/(n_0*r_0) = 1 + u so sin(theta) = sin(theta_0)/(1+u), locking p_active / p_Bouguer = 1.0000x across all 17 radial stations u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive flat-Earth planar Snell law (n(r) * sin(theta) = n_0 * sin(theta_0), which inflates the optical impact parameter by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-shell concentric Eikonal ray-bending quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Planetary limb sunset/sunrise refraction, flattened solar disk mirages, Luneburg/Maxwell fish-eye GRIN spheres, and black-hole photon-sphere raymarching
Conserving Bouguer optical angular momentum p = n(r) * r * sin(theta) so grazing horizon rays bend smoothly around curved planetary shells without false total internal reflection
Updating ray zenith angle in O(1) per spherical shell step via sin(theta) = p / (n(r) * r)
not_for: Microscopic flat microscope slides where radius of curvature R -> infinity
